Mar'dy's last meeting with Tempest lingered on his mind. Curiously as the god left him, he noticed a darkening in the sky. The wind picked up around him, sending debris flying around. The ground felt unsteady and began to quake, the shaking mud liquifying and drawing him in.

#####Tempest has been following Mar'dy which shielded him from the Djiin, now that he is gone, Mar'dy is exposed to the elements. That's the only way I explain the plotholes in my previous stories.

Mar'dy ran as he could through the shallow water, finally reaching dry land. The fierce wind chilled him to the bone. He wrapped his cloak around him and marched inland. Seeing the uprooted trees and earth stripped to the bare rock indicated a long and treacherous time for these lands. The sea was so calm. How strange. Turning back and seeing it in the distance he still felt a calling. "Not yet. They aren't ready."

He kept on. Without having his leg healed this journey may have been a lot more perilous. He soon reached a massive tree uprooted by the wind, the roots pulled out a chunk of earth, exposing a [sheltered crevasse](http://s0.geograph.org.uk/geophotos/02/89/08/2890848_be48c107.jpg). Mar'dy slipped into it. To rest from winds and storm. The fear of earthquakes collapsing the rocks and dirt on him threatened his mind, but the wind was too cold to bear. As he slipped into he noticed the hole got wider the deeper he crawled in. He kept going, curious to see where it ended.

The hole kept getting wider and deeper as he crawled in and soon he was able stand up. How strange he thought. He couldn't see much since the sole source of light was the opening above him. He dared not go much deeper in the dark. So he sat there, hoping that maybe for the storm above him would improve. But it didn't for almost a whole day and curiosity got the better of him. He explored the opening under the tree further, even as the earth shook occasionally, it seemed not to collapse.

As he felt around he noticed the walls getting further from him and his footsteps began to echo more. He called out to see just how big this cave was. The echo lasted for a few seconds. He had stumbled upon a massive cave, but he was in the pitch dark. Any step forward might be an abyss, or a 100 meter drop. Mar'dy decided not to continue, turned around and tried to trace his steps back. But he soon found himself lost. Where was the opening? No way he wandered in this far.

He spent at least another day wandering around, following any paths that followed upwards, but they all turned out to be dead ends. That and wandering in dark caves lead to many painful slips and stubbed toes.

"Now I've done it." He said, plopping himself on the ground.

#####Playing a character with an IQ of like 50.

The spectre sighed at the ridiculousness of the situation. That Lot'dy had only briefly left her sight, and has managed to get completely, and utterly lost. She puzzled at the decisions that would lead the Lot'dy to delve deeper and deeper into the darkness, being able to come up with no satisfactory explanation, she resigned herself to heading into the caves. She told the Saen to wait for her, there was no need to send too many into the cave, especially with the aftershocks still about.

That and the fact that exploring through dark tunnels is a lot easier when you can radiate light, recall your memories at will, and always know the direction your target is in.

It took a few hours, the Lot'dy had managed to head quite far into the cave. Nonetheless the spectre inevitably found her mark curled up in a dead end. She put aside her irritation and decided to beam out a 'smile'.

"Hello little one, what say you that we get out of this place."

Mar'dy could see a faint light start to approach him. He wondered if he was imagining it. He hadn't drank or ate anything in days and his mind faltered. the strange light got closer and closer and stopped in front of him. By now it was almost fully blinding him. Then it said hello.

Mar'dy was not completely surprised. Either this was a hallucination or perhaps another god. It seemed to him, the second you stepped foot outside of the ocean, there were gods suddenly everywhere. Nevertheless he should respond whether hallucination, god or other being.

"I would love to get out of this place. What is your name? I am Mar'dy Kist."

He stood up and strained out his neck, the common way of greeting in the Lot'dy culture.

Lot'dy often had their hands chained or carrying something, so to greet each other they would stand in front of each other and touch necks.

As his eyes adjusted, he soon saw another group trailing behind this glowing creature. Could it be? The same Saen (@GrandPrismatic) that he had met that first fateful night on the beach? His heart was filled suddenly with overwhelming joy.

Diospyra looked quizzically at Mar'dy. Perhaps this being will require more guidance and care than she thought.

"My name is Diospyra, this light will not last forever. It is time that we departed."

Diospyra turned towards the Saen and set out on the return route to the surface, Mar'dy and the shrub-like in tow.

Mar'dy followed his new companion out of cave, delighted to see the Saen but wondered where the others were. Reaching the opening crawling his way out he saw the rest of them and greeted them warmly. He was also pleasantly surprised to see sun out and the weather improved significantly. The only thing on his mind now was his hunger and thirst, which he quickly quenched with a quick drink of a muddy puddle.

"Diospyra, tell me what you are. I could swear I felt your presence that fateful day in the Dire Vents."

"And as a group of companions, we should decide what our next move is. Now that these winds have died down, I fear that things that were once hiding will start to come out, perhaps we cannot stay here for long."

Diospyra smiled. At last, Mar'dy shows promise.

"I agree, many events have been set in motion by unknown perpetrators. Most of these acts could only be achieved by the divine. You, however, seem to have some divinity in your favour. The wave that saved you was much too convenient to have been due to circumstance." Diospyra turned to Mar'dy. "I am neither divine, nor an agent of divinity. I am a lost shadow, a shattered mind, but for all practical purposes I will be your guardian and your guide. I suppose for that purpose I will merely be one of many."

Diospyra stared into her reflection in the water, and suppressed a gasp at what she saw. Behind her shadowy form stood a faint image of the Saen who once was. She tore her gaze away and continued.

"I have been watching you for some time Mar'dy. I was with you at the Dire Vents, I followed you as you were spirited away by the waves. Your ideals have piqued my interest, perhaps, in time, your dream may succeed."

Suddenly, a great beam shone out from the heavens, a ray of golden light. A beam of pure chance. As it contacted the surface, a great wave began spreading through the land. As the front passed over her, Diospyra took in a fragment of its power.

"It would appear, that we have our next destination. That was the direction of the Tree of Life. If we wish to understand what events have transpired, then to that accursed place we must return."

"Then our journey begins."

Mar'dy turned to sea one last time, a twinkling blue sheet in the distance.

"I, gladiator, relinquish my life for this..." he paused for moment, changing the words of the oath he once said every day, "for this world, and what is good in it."

He smiled at his companions and drew his cloak around himself, following the others deeper inland.
